dv.title: ޗައިނާގެ އެސިސްޓެންޓް މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް ރާއްޖެއަށް ކުރެއްވި ރަސްމީ ދަތުރުފުޅު ނިންމަވާލެއްވުމަށްފަހު ފުރާވަޑައިގެންފި
dv.body:
19 ފެބްރުއަރީ 2017، މާލެ،

ޗައިނާގެ އެސިސްޓެންޓް މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒު، ހިޒް އެކްސަލަންސީ މރ. ކޮންގް ޒުއާންޔޫ ރާއްޖެއަށް ކުރެއްވި ތިން ދުވަހުގެ ރަސްމީ ދަތުރުފުޅު ނިންމަވާލެއްވުމަށްފަހު މިއަދު ފުރާވަޑައިގެންފިއެވެ.

އެމަނިކުފާނުގެ މި ދަތުރުފުޅުގައި، ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް އާއި ޗައިނާގެ މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް އާއި ދެމެދު ބޭއްވި 6 ވަނަ މަޝްވަރާ ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި ބައިވެރިވެވަޑައިގެންނެވިއެވެ. މި ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި ދެ ޤައުމުގެ ދެމެދުގައި އުފެންދުންތެރިކަން ކުރިއެރުވުމަށާއި، ޓުއަރިޒަމް ކުރިއެރުވުމަށާއި، އިންސާނީ ވަސީލަތްތައް ކުރިއެރުވުމަށާއި، ޒުވާނުންނާއި ކުޅިވަރުގެ ދާއިރާ އަދި ވިޔަފާރި އިތުރަށް ފުޅާކޮށް ހަރުދަނާކުރުމާ ގުޅޭގޮތުން މަޝްވަރާކުރެވުނެވެ. އަދި ޗައިނާ ސަރުކާރުގެ އެހީގައި މިވަގުތު ރާއްޖޭގައި ކުރިއަށްދާ އެންމެ ބޮޑު ދެ ޕްރޮޖެކްޓްކަމުގައިވާ "މޯލްޑިވްސް-ޗައިނާ ފްރެންޑްޝިޕް ބްރިޖް ޕްރޮޖެކްޓް" އާއި "ވެލާނާ އިންޓަނޭޝަނަލް އެއާޕޯޓް އަޕްގްރޭޑިން ޕްރޮޖެކްޓް" އާއި ގުޅޭ މަޝްވަރާތައްވެސް ކުރެވުނެވެ.  އަދި މި އަހަރަކީ ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާއި ޗައިނާއާ ދެމެދު ސިޔާސީ ގުޅުން ޤާއިމުކުރެވުނުތާ 45 އަހަރުފުރުން ފާހަގަ ކުރާ އަހަރު ކަމަށްވާތީ، މިއަހަރު ކުލަގަދަގޮތެއްގައި ފާހަގަ ކުރުމަށްޓަކައި އެކިއެކި ހަރަކާތްތައް ބޭއްވުމާގުޅޭގޮތުންވެސް މަޝްވަރާކުރެއްވިއެވެ.

މީގެ އިތުރުން އެމަނިކުފާނުގެ މި ދަތުރުފުޅުގައި، ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ، އަލްފާޟިލް ޢަބްދުﷲ ޔާމީން ޢަބްދުލް ޤައްޔޫމްެގެ އަރިހަށް އިޙްތިރާމްގެ ޒިޔާރަތެއްކުރައްވައި އަދި މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް، ޑރ. މުޙައްމަދު އާޞިމް އާ ބައްދަލުކުރައްވައި ދެޤައުމުގެ ދެމެދުގައިވާ ގާތްގުޅުން އިތުރަށް ބަދަހިކޮށް ހަރުދަނާ ކުރުމާ ގުޅޭގޮތުން މަޝްވަރާކުރެއްވިއެވެ.

ޗައިނާގެ އެސިސްޓެންޓް މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެއާޒްގެ މި ދަތުރުފުޅުގައި،  ޗައިނާ ސަރުކާރުގެ އެހީގައި ރާއްޖޭގައި ކުރިއަށްދާ ޕްރޮޖެކްޓް ތަކުގެ ތެރޭގައި ހިމެނޭ "މޯލްޑިވްސް – ޗައިނާ ފްރެންޑްޝިޕް ބްރިޖް ޕްރޮޖެކްޓް" އާއި "ވެލާނާ އިންޓަރނޭޝަނަލް އެއާޕޯޓް އަޕްގްރޭޑިން ޕްރޮޖެކްޓް" އަދި ހުޅުމާލެ "ހައުސިން ޕްރޮޖެކްޓް" ގެ މަސައްކަތް ކުރިއަށްދާގޮތް ބައްލަވާލެއްވިއެވެ.

dv.title: ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް އާއި ޗައިނާގެ މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް އާއި ދެމެދު ބޭއްވުނު 6 ވަނަ މަޝްވަރާ ބައްދަލުވުން
dv.body:
19 ފެބްރުއަރީ 2017، މާލެ،

ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް އާއި ޗައިނާގެ މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް އާއި ދެމެދު ބޭއްވޭ 6 ވަނަ މަޝްވަރާ ބައްދަލުވުން މިއަދު މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒުގައި ގައި ބާއްވާފިއެވެ.

މި ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި ދެ ޤައުމުގެ ދެމެދުގައި އުފެންދުންތެރިކަން ކުރިއެރުވުމަށާއި، ޓުއަރިޒަމް ކުރިއެރުވުމަށާއި، އިންސާނީ ވަސީލަތްތައް ކުރިއެރުވުމަށާއި، ޒުވާނުންނާއި ކުޅިވަރުގެ ދާއިރާ އަދި ވިޔަފާރި އިތުރަށް ފުޅާކޮށް ހަރުދަނާކުރުމާ ގުޅޭގޮތުން މަޝްވަރާކުރެވުނެވެ. އަދި ޗައިނާ ސަރުކާރުގެ އެހީގައި މިވަގުތު ރާއްޖޭގައި ކުރިއަށްދާ އެންމެ ބޮޑު ދެ ޕްރޮޖެކްޓްކަމުގައިވާ "މޯލްޑިވްސް-ޗައިނާ ފްރެންޑްޝިޕް ބްރިޖް ޕްރޮޖެކްޓް" އާއި "ވެލާނާ އިންޓަނޭޝަނަލް އެއާޕޯޓް އަޕްގްރޭޑިން ޕްރޮޖެކްޓް" އާއި ގުޅޭ މަޝްވަރާތައް ކުރެވުނެވެ. އަދި ދެ ޤައުމުގެ ގުޅުން އިތުރަށް ބަދަހިކުރުމާ ގުޅޭގޮތުންވެސް ވަނީ މަޝްވަރާކުރެވިއެވެ. ޗައިނާއަކީ ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ތަރައްޤީގެ މުހިންމު ބައިވެރިއަކަށްވެފައި، ވޭތުވެދިޔަ ތިން އަހަރެއްހާދުވަހުގެ ތެރޭގައިވެސް ރާއްޖޭގެ ތަރައްޤީއަށް ބޮޑެތި އެހތަކެއް ވެދެއްވަމުންގެންދަވާފައިވާތީ އެކަން ފާހަގަކޮށް މިބައްދަލުވުމުގައި ޗައިނާ ސަރުކާރަށް ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރާއި ރައްޔިތުންގެ ނަމުގައި ޝުކުރުއަދާކުރެއްވިއެވެ.

މި އަހަރަކީ ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާއި ޗައިނާއާ ދެމެދު ސިޔާސީ ގުޅުން ޤާއިމުކުރެވުނުތާ 45 އަހަރުފުރުން ފާހަގަ ކުރާ އަހަރު ކަމަށްވާތީ، މިއަހަރު ކުލަގަދަގޮތެއްގައި ފާހަގަ ކުރުމާގުޅޭގޮތުންވެސް މި ބައްދަލުވުމުގައި ޚިޔާލުބަދަލުކޮށް ވާހަކަ ދެކެވުނެވެ.

މި މަޝްވަރާ ބައްދަލުކުރެއްވުމުގައި ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ވަފުދުގެ އިސްބޭފުޅެއްގެ ގޮތުގައި ހުންނެވީ މި މިނިސްޓްރީގެ ސެކްރެޓަރީ ބައިލެޓަރަލް، އަލްފާޟިލް އަޙުމަދު ޚަލީލް އެވެ. ޗައިނާގެ ވަފްދުގައި އިސްކޮށްހުންނެވީ، އެސިސްޓެންޓެ މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް، ހިޒް އެލްސަލަންސީ މރ. ކޮންގް ޒުއާންޔޫ އެވެ.

dv.title: ޗައިނާގެ އެސިސްޓެންޓް މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް ދިވެހި ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރުގެ އަރިހަށް އިޙްތިރާމުގެ ޒިޔާރަތެއް ކުރައްވައިފި
dv.body:
19 ފެބްރުއަރީ 2017، މާލެ،

މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް، ޑރ. މުޙައްމަދު ޢާޞިމް ގެ އަރިހަށް ޗައިނާގެ އެސިސްޓެންޓް މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް، ހިޒް އެކްސަލަންސީ މރ. ކޮންގް ޒުއާންޔޫ އާއި މިއަދު އިޙްތިރާމުގެ ޒިޔާރަތެއް ކުރައްވާފިއެވެ.

މިއަދު މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒުގައި ބޭއްވުނު މި ބައްދަލުކުރެއްވުމުގައި ދެޤައުމުގެ ގުޅުން އިތުރަށް ބަދަހިކޮށް ހަރުދަނާކުރުމާ ގުޅޭގޮތުން ޚިޔާލުބަދަލުކުރައްވައި މަޝްވަރާކުރެއްވިއެވެ. އަދި ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ އިޖްތިމާއީ އަދި އިޤްތިސާދީ ކުރިއެރުވުމަށްޓަކައި ޗައިނާ ސަރުކާރުން ވެދެއްވަމުންގެންދަވާ އެހީތެރިކަމަށް ފޮރިން މިނިސްޓަރ ޑރ މުޙައްމަދު އާޞިމް ޗައިނާ ސަރުކާރަށް ޝުކުރު އަދާކުރެއްވިއެވެ.

މި ބައްދަލުކުރެއްވުމުގައި ސެކްރެޓަރީ، ބައިލެޓަރަލް، އަލްފާޟިލް އަޙުމަދު ޚަލީލް އާއި ޖޮއިންޓް ސެކްރެޓަރީ، އަލްފާޟިލާ އައިޝަތު އަޒީމާ އަދި ޑިރެކްޓަރ، އަލްފާޟިލް އަޙުމަދު ފަޒީލް ބައިވެރިވެވަޑައިގެންނެވިއެވެ.

ޗައިނާގެ އެސިސްޓެންޓް މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެއާޒް، ހިޒް އެކްސަލަންސީ މރ. ކޮންގް ޒުއާންޔޫގެ ޝަރަފުގައި މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް، ޑރ. މުޙައްމަދު ޢާޞިމް މެންދުރުގެ ފަރިއްކޮޅެއް ދެއްވުމަށް ވަނީ ހަމަޖެހިފައިވެއެވެ.

dv.title: ރަސްމީ ދަތުރުފުޅެއްގައި ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު ޗައިނާއަށް ވަޑައިގެންފި
dv.body:
4 ޖެނުއަރީ 2017، ބެއިޖިންގ، ޗައިނާ

ޗައިނާގެ ފޮރިން މިނިސްޓަރު މިސްޓަރ ވަންގ ޔީގެ ދަޢުވަތަކަށް ރާއްޖޭގެ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު ޑރ. މުޙައްމަދު ޢާޞިމް، ރަސްމީ ދަތުރުފުޅެއްގައި މިއަދު ޗައިނާއަށް ވަޑައިގެންފިއެވެ. މިއީ ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރުކަމުގެ މަޤާމާއި ހަވާލުވެ ވަޑައިގެންނެވިފަހުން، ރާއްޖެއާއި ގާތްގުޅުމެއް އޮންނަ ޗައިނާއަށް ޑރ. ޢާޞިމް ކުރައްވާ ފުރަތަމަ ދަތުރުފުޅެވެ.

މިދަތުފުޅުގައި ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު ޑރ. ޢާޞިމް ޗައިނާގެ ފޮރިން މިނިސްޓަރ ހިޒް އެކްސެލެންސީ ވަންގ ޔީގެ އިތުރުން ޗައިނާގެ  ނައިބު ރައީސް ހިޒް އެކްސެލެންސީ މިސްޓަރ ލީ ޔުއާން ޗާއޯއާއި ބައްދަލުކުރެއްވުމަށްވެސް ހަމަޖެހިފައިވެއެވެ. އަދި މިދަތުރުފުޅުގައި "ބެއިޖިންގް ފޮރިން ސްޓަޑީޒް ޔުނިވަރުސިޓީ" ގައި  ރާއްޖެއާއި ޗައިނާއާއި ދެމެދު އޮންނަ ގާތް ގުޅުމާއި ރާއްޖޭގެ ޚާރިޖީ ސިޔާސަތާއި ބެހޭގޮތުން ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރު ޑރ. ޢާޞިމް ތަޤްރީރު ކުރެއްވުމަށްވެސް ހަމަޖެހިފައިވެއެވެ.

ޚާރިޖީ ވަޒީރުގެ މިދަތުރުފުޅުގައި އެވުޒާރާގެ ބައިލެޓެރަލް ސެކެރެޓަރީ އަލްފާޟިލު އަޙުމަދު ޚަލީލް، ވަޒީރުގެ އަރިހުގައި ބައިވެރިވެ ވަޑައިގަންނަވައެވެ.

dv.title: ބަންގްލަދޭޝްގައި މެޑިސިން ކިޔަވަމުންދާ 28 ދިވެހި ދަރިވަރުންނަށް ދިމާވެފައިވާ ރަޖިސްޓްރީ ކުރުމުގެ މައްސަލަައިގައި ދިވެހި ސަފީރު އެކުދިންނާ ބައްދަލުކުރައްވައިފި
dv.body:
23 ޖެނުއަރީ 2017 ، މާލެ،

ބަންގްލަދޭޝްގެ ޗިޓަގޮންގް ޔުނިވަރސިޓީ އޮފް ސައިންސް އެންޑް ޓެކްނޮލޮޖީ ގައި މެޑިސިން ހަދަމުންދާ ދިވެހި ކަޔަވާކުދިންނަށް ދިމާވެފައިވާ ރެޖިސްޓްރޭޝަންގެ މައްސަލައާ ގުޅޭގޮތުން ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ބަންގްލަދޭޝް އަށް ކަނޑައަޅުއްވާފައިހުންނަވާ ސަފީރު އަލްފާޟިލާ އައިޝަތު ޝާން ޝާކިރު މިއަދު އެކުދިންނާ ބައްދަލު ކުރައްވައިފިއެވެ. މި ބައްދަލުކުރެއްވުމުގައި މިމައްސަލައާ ގުޅޭގޮތުން ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރުން ކުރަމުންދާ ކަންތައްތަކުގެ މައުލޫމާތު އެކުދިންނަށް ދެއްވިއެވެ. އަދި މައްސަލަ ހައްލުކުރުމަށް ބަންގްލަދޭޝް ސަރުކާރާއެކު ކުރަމުންގެންދާ މަސައްކަތް ކުރިއަށްގެންދަވާނެ ކަމުގެ ޔަޤީންކަން އެކުދިންނަށް ދެއްވިއެވެ.

ބަންގްލަދޭޝްގައި އަމިއްލަގޮތުން މެޑިސިން ހަދަމުންދާ 28 ދަރިވަރަކަށް ދިމާވެފައިވާ މިމައްސަލަ ވަނީ ބަންގްލަދޭޝްގެ ކަމާބެހޭ ފަރާތްތަކުގެ ސަމާލުކަމަށް އެޤައުމުގެ ފޮރިން މިނިސްޓްރީ މެދުވެރިކޮށް ގެނެސްފައެވެ. އަދި ބަންގްލަދޭޝްގައި ހުންނަ ދިވެހި އެންބަސީން ވަނީ ބަންގްލަދޭޝްގެ ހެލްތް މިނިސްޓރީއާއި ބަންގްލަދޭޝް މެޑިކަލް އެންޑް ޑެންޓަލް ކައުންސިލް އަށް ވެސް މިމައްސަލަ ހުށަހަޅާ އަދި އަވަސް ހައްލެއް ހޯދާދިނުމަށް އެދިފައެވެ. މީގެ އިތުރުންެ ޗިޓަގޮންގް ޔުނިވަރސިޓީ އޮފް ސައިންސް އެންޑް ޓެކްނޮލޮޖީގެ ވައިސް ޗާންސެލަރ އާއި އެންބަސީގެ އޮފިޝަލުން ވާހަކަ ދައްކައި މިކަން މިހާރުން މިހާރަށް ހައްލުކޮއްދެއްވުމަށް ވަނީ އެދިވަޑައިގެންފައެވެ.

ޗިޓަގޮންގް ޔުނިވަރސިޓީ އޮފް ސައިންސް އެންޑް ޓެކްނޮލޮޖީ ގައި މެޑިސިން ހަދާ އެކި ޤައުމު ތަކުގެ ދަރިވަރުން ބަންގްލަދޭޝް މެޑިކަލް އެންޑް ޑެންޓަލް ކައުންސިލްގައި ރަޖިސްޓްރީ ކުރުމުގެ މައްސަލަ މީގެ ކުރިންވެސް ވަނީ ޖެހިފައެވެ. މިގޮތުން 2014 ވަނަ އަހަރު ބަންގްލަދޭޝް މެޑިކަލް އެންޑް ޑެންޓަލް ކައުންސިލްގެ ޤަވައިދު ތަކާ ހިލާފުވެގެން އެ ޔުނިވަރސިޓީ ވަނީ ބަންދުކޮށްފައެވެ. އަދި އަނބުރާ ހުޅުވުމުގެ ހުއްދަ ދެއްވާފައިވަނީ ގިނަ ޝަރުތު ތަކެއް ފުރިހަމަ ކުރުމުންނެވެ.

މިމައްސަލައަށް އަވަސް ހައްލެއްހޯދުމަށް ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރުން ބަންގްލަދޭޝްގެ ކަމާބެހޭ ފަރާތްތަކާ ގުޅިގެން ކުރަމުންގެންދާ މަސައްކަތް ކުރިއަށް ގެންދާނެކަމުގެ ޔަޤީންކަން އަރުވަމެވެ.

dv.title: ކޮމަންވެލްތުން ވަކިވާން ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއިން ނިންމައިފި: ބައިނަލްއަޤްވާމީ ފަރާތްތަކާއި އެކު ކުރިޔަށް އޮތްތަނުގައިވެސް މަސައްކަތްކުރާނެ
dv.description: 13 އޮކްޓޫބަރ 2013، މާލެ ކޮމަންވެލްތުން ވަކިވުމަށް ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރުން މިއަދު ނިންމަވައިފިއެވެ. ކޮމަންވެލްތުން ވަކިވުމަށް ސަރުކާރުން ނިންމެވި ނިންމެވުމަކީ، އުނދަގޫ، އެހެނަސް، ކޮންމެހެން އަޅަންޖެހޭ ފިޔަވަޅެކެވެ. ކޮމަންވެލްތުގައި 1982 ވަނަ އަހަރު، ދިވެހިރާއްޖެ ބައިވެރިވީ، ވަރަށް ފޮނި…
dv.body:
13 އޮކްޓޫބަރ 2013، މާލެ
ކޮމަންވެލްތުން ވަކިވުމަށް ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރުން މިއަދު ނިންމަވައިފިއެވެ. ކޮމަންވެލްތުން ވަކިވުމަށް ސަރުކާރުން ނިންމެވި ނިންމެވުމަކީ، އުނދަގޫ، އެހެނަސް، ކޮންމެހެން އަޅަންޖެހޭ ފިޔަވަޅެކެވެ.
ކޮމަންވެލްތުގައި 1982 ވަނަ އަހަރު، ދިވެހިރާއްޖެ ބައިވެރިވީ، ވަރަށް ފޮނި އުއްމީދުތަކަކާއެކުއެވެ. އެޖަމުއިއްޔާއަކީ މެންބަރު ޤައުމުތަކަށް، ޚާއްސަކޮށް ކުދި ޤައުމުތަކަށް ދިމާވާ މުހިއްމު މައްސަލަތަކުގައި، އެއްބާރުލުމާއި އެހީތެރިކަން ހޯދުމުގެ މަސައްކަތްކުރަން ރަނގަޅު މާޙައުލެއްކަމަށް ދެކިގެންނެވެ.

ދިވެހިސަރުކާރުންވަނީ ކޮމަންވެލްތަށް ފުރިހަމަ އެއްބާރުލުން އެދުނު ކޮންމެ ކަމެއްގައި ފުރިހަމަ އެއްބާރުުން ދީފައެވެ. ކޮމަންވެލްތުން ބަލަން ބޭނުންވި ކޮންމެ ކަމެއްގައި ދެފުށްފެންނަގޮތަށް އެންމެ މަތީ ފެންވަރުގައި ގުޅިގެން ކުރިޔަށް ދިއުމަށް މަސައްކަތްކޮށްފައެވެ. ދިވެހި ސަރުކާރުން އުއްމީދުކުރަމުން ދިޔައީ މިފަދަ އެއްބާރުލުމެއްގެ ސަބަބުން ރާއްޖެއަށް ފައިދާ ކުރަނިވި ނަތީޖާތަކެއް ފެނިގެންދާނެކަމަށެވެ. ނަމަވެސް ހިތާމަޔަކީ، ޑިމޮކްރެސީގެ ސަގާފަތެއް ބިނާކުރުމަށާއި ޑިމޮކްރެޓިކް ނިޒާމެއް ހަރުދަނާކުރުމަށް ކޮށްފައިވާ ގިނަގުނަ މަސައްކަތްތައް ކޮމަންވެލްތުން ބަލައިގެންފައިނުވާކަމެވެ. ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ އަލްފާޟިލް ޢަބްދުﷲ ޔާމީން ޢަބްދުލް ޤައްޔޫމްގެ ސަރުކާރުންވަނީ 110 ޤާނޫނެއް ފާސްކޮށްފައެވެ. މީގެތެރެއިން 94 ޤާނޫނަކީ ސީދާ ކޮމަންވެލްތުގެ މައިގަނޑު އަސާސްތަކާ ގުޅޭ ޤާނޫނުތަކެކެވެ. މިޤާނޫނުތަކުގެ ތެރެއިން 69 ޤާނޫނަކީ އިންސާނީ ޙައްޤުތައް ކަށަވަރުކުރުމަށާއި ޑިމޮކްރެޓިކް ގަވަރނަންސް ހަރުދަނާކުރުމަށާއި، ދައުލަތުގެ ބާރުތައް ވަކިކުރުމަށް ވާގިދޭ ޤާނޫނުތަކެކެވެ. މިކަންތައްތަކުގު ސަބަބުން ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގައި ޤާނޫނުގެ ވެރިކަމާއި ސަރުކާރު ހިންގުމާބެހޭ ނިޒާމު އިތުރަށް ހަރުދަނާވެ، ނަތީޖާތައް ދަނީ ފެންނަމުންނެވެ.
ފެބްރުއަރީ 2012 ގައި އޭރުގެ ރައީސް އިސްތިއުފާ ދެއްވުމާއިއެކު، ކޮމަންވެލްތުން ވަނީ ރާއްޖެއާ ދެކޮޅަށް ފިޔަވަޅު އަޅާފައެވެ. ރާއްޖޭގެ ވެރިކަން ބަދަލުވެފައިވަނީ ދުސްތޫރީ ހަމަތަކުގެ މަތިންކަމަށް، ކޮމަންވެލްތުގެ އެހީއާއެކު އެކުލަވާލެވުނު ކޮމިޝަން އޮފް ނޭޝަނަލް އިންކުއައިރީން ނިންމިނަމަވެސް، ކޮމަންވެލްތުން ރާއްޖެއާމެދު އެކި ފެންވަރުގެ ފިންތުންތައް ކުރިމަތިކުރުވިއެވެ. ރާއްޖެއާމެދު އަމަލުކޮށްފައިވަނީ ހަމައާއި އިންސާފުން ބޭރުންނެވެ. ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާމެދު ފިޔަވަޅު އަޅައި، ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ ދާޚިލީ ސިޔާސަތުތަކަށް ބާރުފޯރުވުމަށް މަސައްކަތްކުރަމުންދިޔައީ، ކޮމަންވެލްތުގެ ޗާޓަރާއި އދ. ޗާޓަރުގެ އަސާސްތަކާއިވެސް ޚިލާފަށެވެ. ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭއަކީ ބައިނަލްއަޤްވާމީ މަސްރަޙުގައި މަޤްބޫލުކަން ލިބިފައިވާ، ކުޑަ ޤައުމަކަށްވާތީ، ކޮމަންވެލްތް މިނިސްޓީރިއަލް އެކްޝަން ގްރޫޕުންނާއި ކޮމަންވެލްތް ސެކްރެޓޭރިއަޓުން ޑިމޮކްރަސީ ކުރިއެރުވުމުގެ ނަމުގައި ރާއްޖެއަށް އުނދަގޫތަކެއް ފޯރުވައި، ބައިނަލްއަޤްވާމީ މަސްރަޙުގައި އެޖަމިއްޔާއަކީ މުހިންމު، ބަސްވިކޭ ޖަމުއިއްޔާއަކަށް ހެދުމަށެވެ.
ދިވެހިރާއްޖެ ކޮމަންވެލްތުން ވަކިވިނަމަވެސް، ދިވެހިސަރުކާރުން ބޭރުގެ ފަރާތްތަކާއެކު، ޚާއްސަކޮށް ރާއްޖެއަށް ހެޔޮއެދޭ ރާއްޖެއާއި ގުޅިގެން މަސައްކަތްކުރަން ތިބި ޤައުމުތަކާއި ޖަމިއްޔާތަކާއެކު އަބަދުވެސް މަސައްކަތްކުރަމުންގެންދާނެއެވެ.

dv.title: ދިވެހިރާއްޖެ އާއި ޗައިނާ ދެމެދު އުފެދިފައިވީ ގުޅުން ވޭތުވި އަހަރުތަކުތެރޭ އިތުރަށް ހަރުދަނާވެފައިވާ ކަމުގައި މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް ވަގުތީގޮތުން ހިންގެވުމާއި ހަވާލުވެހުންނެވި އަލްފާޟިލާ އިރުތިޝާމް އާދަމް ވިދާޅުވެއްޖެ
dv.body:
29 ސެޕްޓެމްބަރ 2016

ދިވެހިރާއްޖެއާއި ޗައިނާ އާއި ދެމެދު އުފެދިފައިވާ ގުޅުން ވޭތުވެދިއަ އަހަރުތަކުތެރޭ އިތުރަށް ހަރުދަނާވެފައިވާކަމުގައި މިނިސްޓްރީ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް ވަގުތީގޮތުން ހިންގެވުމާއި ހަވާލުވެހުންނެވި އަލްފާޟިލާ އިރުތިޝާމް އާދަމް ވިދާޅުވިއެވެ. އެކަަމަނާ މިހެންވިދާޅުވީ ޗައިނާ އެމްބަސީ އިން އިންތިޒާމްކޮށްގެން ހޮޓެލް ޖެންގައި ބޭއްވި އެޤައުމުގެ 67ވަނަ ޤައުމީދުވަހުގެ މުނާސަބަތުގައި ބޭއްވި ރަސްމިއްޔާތުގައި ވާހަކަފުޅު ދައްކަވަމުންނެވެ.

އެކަމަނާގެ ވާހަކަފުޅުގައި ރާއްޖޭގެ ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާ، އަލްފާޟިލް ޢަބްދުﷲ ޔާމީން އަބްދުލް ގައްޔޫމްގެ ނަންފުޅުގައި ޗައިނާގެ ރައީސް ޝީ ޖިންޕިންގް އަށާއި އެޤައުމުގެ ރައްޔިތުންނަށް ޤައުމީދުވަހުގެ ތަހުނިއާ ދެންނެވިއެވެ. މީގެ އިތުރުން  ދެ ޤައުމުގެ ދެމެދުގައި އުފެދިފައިވާ ހަރުދަނާ ގުޅުންތަކަށް އަލިއަޅުއްވާލައްވާ ޗައިނާ އިން ދެއްވާ ދީލަތި އެހީތަކަށް ޝުކުރު އަދާކުރައްވިއެވެ. އަދި ޗައިނާ –މޯލްޑިވްސް ފްރެންޑްޝިޕް ބްރިޖް އަކީ މި ދެ ޤައުމުގެ ގާތްގުޅުން ދައްކަވައިދޭ ރަމްޒެއްކަމުގައިވެސް ފާހަގަ ކުރެއްވިއެވެ.

en.title: Speech by Foreign Minister at the Inaugural Reception of the Embassy of Japan in Maldives
en.body:
8 February 2016, Male' - 74/2016,

Bismillahi- Rahmani Rahim
Your Excellency Mr. Masakazu Hamachi, Parliamentary Vice Minister for Foreign Affairs of Japan,
Your Excellency Ambassador Suganuma,
Ministers, Members of Parliament,
Distinguished Guests, Ladies and Gentlemen,

Assalaamalaikum, konbanwa and very good evening to you all
Tonight as we gather to celebrate the joyous occasion of the opening of the Embassy of Japan in the Maldives, I wish to congratulate the Government and friendly people of Japan and welcome this important milestone in the close relations between our two counties. The opening of the Embassy is the beginning of a new chapter in the strong bonds between the governments and the peoples of Maldives and Japan; I am privileged and honoured to be part of this important event. I have the honour to warmly welcome, His Excellency Masakazu Hamachi, Parliamentary Vice Minister of Japan.
Excellencies, Ladies and Gentlemen,

Formal diplomatic ties between the two countries began in 1967, nearly fifty years ago. Our relationship however, has its anchor way back in the Fifteenth Century on something that is very special to our two peoples - “Katsuobushi” (dried Bonito), known as “Hikimas” in the Maldives. According to the history of “Katsuobushi,” Katsuobushi originated in the Maldives in the late Fourteenth Century and was introduced to Japan in the early Fifteenth Century from the Maldives. While Hikimas remains an important ingredient in Maldivian cooking, I understand that Katsuobushi is essentially the base of Japanese cuisine as well.

Since the beginning of official diplomatic ties, our relationship has grown from strength to strength. Japan has been a true and a well-respected friend who has always stood by us during times of need. The development assistance we have received from the friendly people of Japan has contributed immensely to the socio-economic development of our country. From human resources development to environmental protection, sustainable fisheries to modern day communications and transport, electrification, health sector development as well as humanitarian and reconstruction assistance in the aftermath of the devastating Asian Tsunami of 2004, Japanese assistance has virtually reached all four corners of the Maldivian archipelago. I can say quite confidently that, there isn’t a single Maldivian who has not benefited, either directly or indirectly, from the generosity of Japan over the years. I can very proudly say that every yen that Japan has given us has reached its intended target and has contributed directly to the betterment of the livelihoods of our people.

Excellencies, Ladies and Gentlemen,

As we celebrate this historic milestone in the relations between our two countries, we are reminded of the official visit of President Yameen to Japan in 2014. That was the first time that a head of state from the Maldives visited Japan on the official invitation of the Japanese Government. That was also the first official visit of President Yameen to any country outside of the South Asia region.

During the visit, Prime Minister Shinzo Abe and President Yameen agreed on a new stage of cooperation based on over forty years of friendship and trust. I have no doubt; the opening of the Embassy is clearly a direct outcome of this renewed friendship and cooperation.

Since the President’s visit, we have witnessed increased high-level exchanges between the two countries including greater cooperation amongst parliamentarians. I too have had the pleasure of making an official visit to Japan last year and meet with Prime Minister Abe and Foreign Minister Kishida. I sincerely hope that such high-level exchanges will increase with the opening of the Embassy and would pave way for a visit of the Prime Minister and the Foreign Minister to the Maldives in the not so distant future.

Excellencies, Ladies and Gentlemen,

On behalf of the Government, let me take this opportunity to thank the Government and the friendly people of Japan for the most generous support and cooperation extended to the Maldives over the years and most importantly for being a true and a reliable friend. Let me also take this opportunity to reiterate the firm commitment of the Government of Maldives to its relations with Japan.

Before I conclude, let me assure Ambassador Suganuma of our firm commitment and readiness of my staff and I, to working closely with Your Excellency as we strive to strengthen relations between our two countries.

I wish Japan-Maldives relations every success.

Wassalaamalaikumwarahmathullah
Domo arigatogozaimasu (thank you very much)

The High Commissioner expressed Maldivian Government’s desire to further strengthen the excellent relations, and noted that the President and the Government wishes to exchange more frequent high level visits to foster the bilateral relation of the two countries.

The High Commissioner also noted that the Government of Maldives places great importance to take the relationship between the two countries to new heights and stressed the need for an easy visa regime between the two countries. In this regard, the High Commissioner recalled the meeting between the Minister of Foreign Affairs of Malaysia H. E. Dato Sri Anifah Aman and Minister of Foreign Affairs of Maldives H. E. Ms. Dunya Maumoon, in Jeddah during which the same issue were discussed. An easy visa regime will resolve most of the visa issues that most Maldivians faces now.

In the meeting both the High Commissioner and the Prime Minister discussed ways to further strengthen the relations between the two countries, especially in the fields of social and economic development and also health and educational sector.

In conclusion the High Commissioner indicated that the Government of Maldives is confident that the relations between the two countries would remain outstanding in the future as well and that Maldives would receive the same level of support and assistance from Malaysia as a brotherly Muslim Country.

en.title: Minister Dunya sends Independence Day greetings to Sri Lanka

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“On the Sixty-Eighth Anniversary of Sri Lanka’s Independence, it is with great pleasure that I extend my heartiest congratulations and sincere best wishes to Your Excellency, the Government and the friendly people of Sri Lanka.

Maldives and Sri Lanka enjoys strong bilateral ties of friendship. en.body:
03 February 2016, Male'

Minister of Foreign Affairs, Her Excellency Dunya Maumoon has sent a message of sympathy to His Excellency Salahuddin Rabbani, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Afghanistan, condemning the attack in Kabul, outside an office of the civil order Police, causing loss of several lives and injury to many.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“It was with deep shock and horror that I learnt the news of the suicide bomb attack in Kabul, outside an office of the civil order police, causing loss of several innocent lives and injury to many more.

The Maldives strongly condemns these cowardly acts of terror and all acts of violence perpetuated against innocent people. We are fully committed to the fight against terrorism and we will continue to work closely with the Government of Afghanistan and the whole international community in eliminating this global menace.

At this time of great national distress and mourning, the Government and the people of Maldives join me in conveying profound sympathy to the members of the bereaved families, the Government and the people of Afghanistan.

en.title: Maldives Mission participated at the 24th Session of the Working Group of the Universal Periodic Review
en.body:
29 January 2016, Geneva, Switzerland

The Working Group of the Universal Periodic Review concluded its 24th Session in Geneva this afternoon. Fourteen member states were reviewed at this session. - namely: Namibia, Niger, Mozambique, Estonia, Paraguay, Belgium, Denmark, Palau, Somalia, Seychelles, Solomon Islands, Latvia, Sierra Leone and Singapore. The Maldives delivered statements and recommendations for seven countries. - Denmark, Palau, Somalia, Seychelles, Solomon Islands, Sierra Leone and Singapore. The recommendations made by Maldives focused on a broad range of issues – gender equality, health, persons with disabilities, climate change, education, water, among other important human rights.

The Maldives was part of the troika together with Botswana and Ecuador at the review of Singapore, and delivered the statement as the rapporteur at the adoption of the report of the Working Group.

The Maldives is represented at the 24th Session of the UPR Working Group by Her Excellency Dr. Hala Hameed, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary and Permanent Representative of Maldives to the United Nations Office at Geneva and Ms. Rishfa Rasheed, Counsellor of the Permanent Mission.

UPR Working Group holds sessions thrice a year, in January, May and October. This is the final year of the second cycle of the reviews, where all 193 member states of the UN are reviewed based on their human rights situation.

In his statement at the Security Council’s quarterly open debate, he also called upon Israel to take concrete actions towards ending its occupation and paving the way for a two state solution.

The Maldives strongly condemned the unwarranted restrictions imposed by Israel in the occupied territory of Palestine; including the West Bank, Gaza Strip and East Jerusalem. The Maldives also reiterated support for Palestine on their journey to becoming a full member state of the United Nations.

During the open debate on the situation in the Middle East, including the Palestinian question, the Maldives also condemned the recent attack on the Embassy of Saudi Arabia in Iran, and also the terrorist attacks in Beirut in November by ISIL.

Member States that spoke at the open debate convened by Uruguay as the current President of the Council, highlighted the absence of progress towards a political solution to the conflicts in the Middle East. They further expressed concern on the continued incidents of violence between Israel and Palestine and urged for an early resumption of talks between them.

en.title: Maldives Foreign Minister criticises Mohamed Nasheed activities abroad: ‘It has gone from medical leave to media leave.’
en.body:
25 January 2016

- Nasheed has politicised medical leave trip to UK
- Multiple engagements show former President has been ‘disingenuous at best and misleading at worst’ about his medical condition
- Despite claiming to represent freedom of speech, Nasheed’s American PR media team are vetting attendees for a London press conference on Monday to remove critical voices – including refusal to accept a High Commission official
- Maldives Government reminds the international community not to forget Nasheed is convicted of ordering to abduct a judge, which carries strict penalties in any country.

MALE’ – The Maldives Foreign Minister Dunya Maumoon today has criticised former President Mohamed Nasheed for exploiting the terms of a 30-day medical release to embark on a lobbying and media campaign abroad.

Mr Nasheed made a direct request to the Government for a temporary release to undergo surgery for a back ailment. Despite the medical expertise being available in the Maldives, the government granted a temporary release for Mr Nasheed to seek treatment in the United Kingdom.

The Maldives government acted in good faith during the negotiations over Mr Nasheed’s release; similarly it has not sought to politicise what was seen as an important step to ensure Mr Nasheed’s good health is maintained.

However, since Mr Nasheed’s arrival in London, his party, aids and advisors have organised multiple meetings and media engagements with the sole aim of politicising his trip. Mr Nasheed’s ability to undergo this busy itinerary undermines the notion that his medical condition is grave enough to warrant treatment abroad.

The Government also notes its profound disappointment that a member of its London High Commission was denied entry to Mr Nasheed’s forthcoming London Press Conference by his American PR team, despite a request many days in advance. This is in stark contrast to the unimpeded access given to the press conferences of Mrs Amal Clooney and Mr Nasheed’s US advisers during their last visit to the Maldives.

Finally, the government would like to remind its international partners, the media and other stakeholders of the serious charges facing Mr Nasheed. The arrest of a Criminal Court Judge is a grave abuse of executive office – and is something he has admitted to ordering. A Supreme Court appeal is underway and the Government hopes the former President respects the legal channels made available to him to challenge his conviction.

Commenting, the Foreign Minster of the Maldives Dunya Maumoon said:

‘It is now clear the former President has been disingenuous at best, and misleading at worst, in seeking medical leave in the UK. The Government acted in good faith in allowing Mr Nasheed to travel abroad for treatment. Yet it is now clear his primary goal was to court publicity in the United Kingdom. This is not medical leave, but media leave.

‘Mr Nasheed’s PR advisers’ vetting of attendees at his press conference reveals, as many in the Maldives witnessed during his tenure as President, that he does not practice what he preaches when it comes to freedom of speech.

‘No amount of PR stunts will alter the fact that Mr Nasheed lost an election that was recognised as in line with international standards by the EU, amongst others. Neither will it change the fact that Mr Nasheed ordered the arrest of a senior judge – a serious crime that he admitted to himself in a BBC interview – the charge in which he was convicted. The judge in question had released one of Nasheed’s most vocal critics: that he was then arrested puts pay to the idea that Mr. Nasheed believes in freedom of expression.

‘The opportunity for Mr Nasheed to clear his name remains in the Maldives, not in the TV studios of London or Los Angeles. The Supreme Court appeal in Mr Nasheed’s conviction will continue while he meets politicians and the media in London. We look forward to his return and wish him speedy recovery from his medical treatment.’

en.title: Statement by Minister of Foreign Affairs H E Dunya Maumoon at the OIC Extraordinary Meeting of the Council of Foreign Ministers Jeddah, 21 January 2016
en.description: In the name of Allah, the most beneficent, the most merciful Peace be upon our prophet Mohamed Sallallahu Alaihi Wasallam, his family and his companions Mr. Chairman, Mr. Secretary General, Excellencies AssalamAlaikum Warahmathullahi Wabarakathuh,
en.body:
In the name of Allah, the most beneficent, the most merciful
Peace be upon our prophet Mohamed Sallallahu Alaihi Wasallam, his family and his companions
Mr. Chairman, Mr. Secretary General, Excellencies
AssalamAlaikum Warahmathullahi Wabarakathuh,

I would like to express my sincere appreciation to all delegations who have expressed their support in convening this Extraordinary Meeting of the Council of Foreign Ministers. Allow me to congratulate the Foreign Minister of Kuwait and the OIC Secretary General for convening this Extraordinary Meeting. We are here today to discuss the aggression on the diplomatic mission of Saudi Arabia in Tehran and the Saudi Consulate in Mashhad in the Islamic Republic of Iran and on the cause of Palestine and Al-Quds Al-Shareef.

Excellencies:

President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom and his Government and the people of Maldives strongly condemn the atrocious manner at which the Saudi Embassy and the Consulate were attacked by Iranian protesters. We extend our support to the Government of Saudi Arabia. An attack on diplomatic and consular Mission is of grave concern. And the failure to prevent these attacks by the host country represents a serious breach of two of the most important international conventions that we all pledge to abide by.

The Maldives calls upon the Government of Iran to take all necessary steps to ensure that the perpetrators of these atrocious crimes are brought to justice. We also call upon the Government of Iran to respect the international conventions by ensuring diplomatic and consular privileges and uphold the rights entitled.

Allow me to recall the fundamental principle of the inviolability of diplomatic and consular premises. The host Government has a solemn responsibility to take all necessary steps to protect and safeguard diplomatic and consular premises against any damage. The inactivity to do so is a clear violation of the Diplomatic, and Consular Relations Conventions.

Excellencies,

Islam is not only a religion; it is a civilization; one that teaches and promotes peace, tolerance, compassion, and above all, modernity. To enjoy the glory of the true values of Islam, we, the Muslims, should stand united. We should adhere to the principles of OIC Charter that obligates us not to interfere in the domestic affairs of our Member States. It requires us to respect sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity of each Member State. Our unity as a Muslim Ummah depends entirely on the stability in our countries.

Excellencies,

Ignorance promotes intolerance, which leads to radicalism, and radicalism breeds terrorism. The greatest challenge facing the Muslim Ummah today is terrorism carried out in the name of Islam. The Maldives condemns terrorism in all its forms and manifestations. And we call upon countries of the world to take a strategic decision to promote a culture of respect in their societies as a tool to fight against the menace of terrorism.

Excellencies:

The Maldives continues to be concerned over the situation in Palestine. President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom and the Government of Maldives condemn Israel’s illegal settlements in Palestine. We call on countries around the world, to support the State of Palestine with East Jerusalem as its capital and to recognize its sovereignty in Palestinian territories in the pre-1967 borders. Maldives believes Al-Quds is an integral part of the Palestinian Territory.

The Maldives supports the peaceful resolution of conflicts and we are confident that this would lead to strengthening the global fight against terrorism. The Maldives does not believe that the use of violence to achieve religious or political goals is justifiable in any circumstances. Violence is not the answer to disagreements. Instead, tolerance, dialogue, and collaboration must be the means for resolving our differences. Let us not allow chaos to rise in our societies due to our differences. Let us hold hands and unite to combat terrorism and ensure peace in our Ummah.

Thank you.

WassalamAlaikumWarahmathullahiWabarakathuh.

The host Government has a solemn responsibility to take all necessary steps to protect and safeguard diplomatic and consular premises against any damage. The inactivity to do so is a clear violation of the Diplomatic, and Consular Relations Conventions.

Excellencies,

Islam is not only a religion; it is a civilization; one that teaches and promotes peace, tolerance, compassion, and above all, modernity. To enjoy the glory of the true values of Islam, we, the Muslims, should stand united. We should adhere to the principles of OIC Charter that obligates us not to interfere in the domestic affairs of our Member States. It requires us to respect sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity of each Member State. Our unity as a Muslim Ummah depends entirely on the stability in our countries.

Excellencies,

Ignorance promotes intolerance, which leads to radicalism, and radicalism breeds terrorism. The greatest challenge facing the Muslim Ummah today is terrorism carried out in the name of Islam. The Maldives condemns terrorism in all its forms and manifestations. And we call upon countries of the world to take a strategic decision to promote a culture of respect in their societies as a tool to fight against the menace of terrorism.

Excellencies:

The Maldives continues to be concerned over the situation in Palestine. President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom and the Government of Maldives condemn Israel’s illegal settlements in Palestine. We call on countries around the world, to support the State of Palestine with East Jerusalem as its capital and to recognize its sovereignty in Palestinian territories in the pre-1967 borders. Maldives believes Al-Quds is an integral part of the Palestinian Territory.

The Maldives supports the peaceful resolution of conflicts and we are confident that this would lead to strengthening the global fight against terrorism. The Maldives does not believe that the use of violence to achieve religious or political goals is justifiable in any circumstances. Violence is not the answer to disagreements. Instead, tolerance, dialogue, and collaboration must be the means for resolving our differences. Let us not allow chaos to rise in our societies due to our differences. Let us hold hands and unite to combat terrorism and ensure peace in our Ummah.

Thank you.

WassalamAlaikumWarahmathullahiWabarakathuh.

en.title: Maldives condemns the attacks on the Embassy of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and its Consulate in Iran
en.body:
21 January 2016, Male’

The Maldives has strongly condemned the attacks on the Embassy of Saudi Arabia in Tehran and its Consulate in Mashhad. In a statement delivered by Minister of Foreign Affairs H.E. Ms. Dunya Maumoon, at the Extraordinary Meeting of the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers on Cause of Aggressions on Saudi Diplomatic Missions in the Islamic Republic of Iran, Maldives echoed its support to the Government of Saudi Arabia.

Minister Dunya stated that an attack on a diplomatic Mission is of grave concern and the failure to prevent these attacks by the host country represents a serious breach to two of the most important international conventions that we pledged to abide by. The Maldives also called upon the Government of Iran to take all necessary steps to ensure that the perpetrators of these atrocious crimes are brought to justice.

In her statement, Minister Dunya also condemned the illegal Israeli settlement in Palestine and call on countries around the world, to support the State of Palestine with East Jerusalem as its capital and to recognize its sovereignty in Palestinian territories in the pre-1967 borders. She further stated that the greatest challenge facing the Muslim Ummah today in the terrorist activities carried out in the name of Islam, the religion of compassion.

Continuing with her statement Minister Dunya expressed that Islam is a civilization, one that teaches and promotes peace, tolerance, compassion, and above all, modernity. She called upon countries of the world to take a strategic decision to promote a culture of respect in their societies as a tool to fight against the menace of terrorism and to work together and face common challenges as one Ummah.

Concluding her statement Minister Dunya stated that the Maldives supports the peaceful resolution of conflicts and is confident that this would lead to strengthening the global fight against terrorism. The Maldives does not believe that the use of violence to achieve religious or political goals is justifiable in any circumstances. Said Minister Dunya

The Maldives delegation to the Extraordinary Meeting is headed by Minister Dunya who is accompanied by H.E. Mr. Abdullah Hameed, Ambassador of Maldives to Saudi Arabia and Mr. Ibrahim Shaheeb, Additional Secretary at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

ENDS

en.title: Maldives appointed as Co-Chair of the Steering Committee on Partnerships for Small Island Developing States
en.description: On 20 January 2016, the President of the United Nations General Assembly has appointed H.E. Mr. Ahmed Sareer, the Permanent Representative of the Republic of Maldives as Co-Chair for the Steering Committee on Partnerships for Small Island Developing States through a letter dated 20 January 2016.…
en.body:
On 20 January 2016, the President of the United Nations General Assembly has appointed H.E. Mr. Ahmed Sareer, the Permanent Representative of the Republic of Maldives as Co-Chair for the Steering Committee on Partnerships for Small Island Developing States through a letter dated 20 January 2016. H.E. Mr. Sebastiano Cardi, the Permanent Representative of Italy was appointed as the other Co-Chair of the Committee.

The mandate of the Co-Chairs is to follow up on the implementation of the (SIDS) Accelerated Modalities of Action (SAMOA) Pathway and the Mauritius Strategy for the Implementation of the Programme of Action for the Sustainable Development of Small Island Developing States.

The Maldives is continuing to play a prominent role in its second year as the Chair of the Alliance of Small Island States (AOSIS) in leading the voice of SIDS through intergovernmental negotiations in Climate Change and Sustainable Development.

ENDS

en.title: Foreign Minister Dunya sends message of sympathy to the Foreign Minister of Pakistan
en.body:
20 January 2016 - Male’

Minister of Foreign Affairs, Her Excellency Dunya Maumoon has sent a message of sympathy to His Excellency Sartaj Aziz, the Advisor to the Prime Minister on Foreign Affairs of Pakistan, condemning the attack at Bacha Khan University in Charsadda, causing loss of several lives and injury to many.

Minister’s message reads as follows:

“It was with great shock and sadness that I learnt the news of the brutal attack at Bacha Khan University in Charsadda, causing loss of several lives and injury to many. The Government and the people of Maldives condemn this violent act of terror in strongest terms.

At this time of great national distress and mourning, the Government and the people of Maldives join me in conveying profound sympathy to the members of the bereaved families, Excellency, the Government and the people of Pakistan. The Maldives strongly condemns these cowardly acts of terror and all acts of violence perpetuated against innocent people. We are fully committed to the fight against terrorism and we will continue to work closely with the Government of Pakistan and the whole international community in eliminating this global menace.

Please accept, Excellency, the assurances of my highest consideration.”

ENDS

en.title: Our conversation today has once again assured that as a nation we have moved forward more quickly and more ambitiously, says Attorney General
en.body:
19 January 2016, Geneva, Switzerland

While illustrating the Maldives progress in promotion and protection of children at the Committee on the Rights of the Child, the Attorney General HE. Mohamed Anil has underscored that the Maldives has demonstrated its full commitment to perform in line with the provisions and principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child. We have ensured a robust and a progressive system of child development.

The Attorney General made the statement in his closing remarks at the review of the fourth and fifth combined report of the Maldives under the Convention on the Rights of the Child held in Geneva today. Attorney General also stated that ‘We came here with a sincere intent to listen, to engage, and share our experiences as well as the formidable challenges we encounter. More significantly, to listen to your concerns and to be guided by the experiences and recommendations shared with us. Continuing with his closing remarks AG further said that ‘Our conversation today has once again assured that as a nation we have moved forward more quickly and more ambitiously.

During his statement the Attorney General also thanked the members of the committee who took the time to pose questions and clarifications and welcomed them in the spirit of dialogue and engagement.

In concluding, Attorney General also acknowledged representatives of civil society, who have contributed to the Parallel Reports submitted to the Committee. Attorney General reaffirmed the Government’s commitment towards continuing to make the life of  Maldivian children brighter.

The Maldives delegation to the Convention on the Rights of the Child was led by H.E Attorney General Mohamed Anil, Foreign Secretary  H.E Dr. Ali Naseer Mohamed and Permanent Representative of Maldives in Geneva, H.E Dr. Hala Hameed, Mrs. Mariyam Azra Ahmed, Minister of State for Law and Gender, Mrs. Fathimath Azza, Director General of Ministry of Education, Mrs. Hawwa Shafeea Riza, Senior State attorney at Attorney General’s Office, Ms. Rishfa Rasheed, Counsellor at the Maldives Mission in Geneva, Mrs. Aishath Rishmee, Assistant Director of Ministry of Law and Gender, Mr. Abdulla Ashraf, Assistant Director of Ministry of Law and Gender and Ms. Laila Shareef, Senior Desk Officer at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

ENDS

en.title: The President’s pledge to champion child rights at national and international levels is not because it is an obligation; but because it is the right thing to do” Attorney General Anil
en.body:
19 January 2016, Geneva, Switzerland

Speaking to the Committee on Convention on the Rights of the Child, Attorney General H.E. Mohamed Anil highlighted the extraordinary progress that the Maldives has made on promoting and protecting the rights of the child. The Maldives was reviewed today at the 71st Session of the Committee on the Rights of the Child of the United Nations Human Rights Council.

Placing the progress of Maldives within the contextual legislative framework, Attorney General outlined Government’s ambition to strengthen the legal protection for the children. In this regard, he pressed that the new Child Protection Bill, Juvenile Justice Bill and Gender Equality Bill will harmonize the existing child protection laws. Attorney General also highlighted on the high enrolment rate for primary and secondary education, low maternal and infant mortality rates and the improved state care for children. Attorney General further reflected on the new challenges that the fast pace of change has brought on, which the society is not entirely accustomed to deal with. Attorney General expressed the commitment of the Government of President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom’s, to continue improving the child protection system through realising their aspirations and hopes.

Speaking of the achievements that the Maldives has made over the eighteen years since its initial review, the Attorney General noted that President Yameen’s commitment to child protection will be guided by the Sustainable Development Goals adopted last September. Attorney General further announced that Maldives will remain steadfast in its commitment to safeguard the rights of children.

The Maldives delegation to the Convention on the Rights of the Child was led by H.E Attorney General Mohamed Anil, Foreign Secretary H.E Dr. Ali Naseer Mohamed and Permanent Representative of Maldives in Geneva, H.E Dr. Hala Hameed, Mrs. Mariyam Azra Ahmed, Minister of State for Law and Gender, Mrs. Fathimath Azza, Director General of Ministry of Education, Mrs. Hawwa Shafeea Riza, Senior State attorney at Attorney General’s Office, Ms. Rishfa Rasheed, Counsellor at the Maldives Mission in Geneva, Mrs. Aishath Rishmee, Assistant Director of Ministry of Law and Gender, Mr. Abdulla Ashraf, Assistant Director of Ministry of Law and Gender and Ms. Laila Shareef, Senior Desk Officer at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Ends

en.title: Former President of the Maldives Mohamed Nasheed leaves to UK for medical treatment
en.body:
18 January 2016, Male'

- Former President, currently serving a jail sentence, has left the Maldives to the UK for medical treatment.

- Before leaving the Maldives, Mr Nasheed signed an undertaking to return to the Maldives after completing his medical treatment.
- Mr Nasheed’s brother signed a document as a guarantor.

- Government of the Maldives notes President Nasheed himself requested travel to UK, government agreed to accommodate request.

Former President of Maldives, Mr Mohamed Nasheed has left the Maldives this evening to the UK to undergo medical treatment. Earlier, the former President had requested the Government to grant him permission to travel to the UK for treatment, which the relevant authorities of the Government granted.

The former President Mohamed Nasheed has signed the standard guarantee document agreeing to return to the Maldives, to serve the remainder of his sentence following the completion of the medical treatment in the United Kingdom. Mr Nasheed’s brother is acting as guarantor during his stay abroad.

The government of the Maldives would like to reiterate that the former President is a serving prisoner and must abide by the laws of the Maldives.  An appeal against his conviction is pending before the Supreme Court and unless and until the court rules otherwise he is required to serve the remainder of his sentence.

The Government would like to highlight that it was former President Nasheed himself who requested to undergo surgery in the UK. The Government agreed to accommodate his request.

Foreign Minister Dunya Maumoon stated: ‘It is standard procedure for any prisoner who applies to travel abroad, for medical treatment, to sign a guarantee. All prisoners who have travelled abroad have signed such documents as required by Maldivian law. This rule has been in existence before Mr Nasheed came to office, and has not been introduced in an ad hoc manner.

‘I am glad all relevant legal documentation is completed. Throughout this period the government has acted in good faith. We ask that Mr Nasheed and his representatives in turn abide by the agreement signed and agreed today. These are standard requirements in line with international norms.’

ENDS

en.title: Minister of State, The Rt. Hon. Hugo Swire depart after concluding his official visit to the Maldives
en.body:

dv.title: މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް އ.ދ. ގެ ސެކްރެޓަރީ ޖެނެރަލްއާ ބައްދަލުކުރައްވައިފި
dv.body:
ނިއުޔޯކް: 23 ސެޕްޓެމްބަރ 2016

މިނިސްޓަރ އޮފް ފޮރިން އެފެއާޒް ޑޮކްޓަރ މުޙައްމަދު ޢާސިމް، އ.ދ. ގެ ސެކްރެޓަރީ ޖެނެރަލް މިސްޓަރ ބާންކި މޫން އާ މިއަދު ބައްދަލު ކުރައްވައިފިއެވެ. މިބައްދަލުވުން އޮތީ އދ. ގެ މައި މަރުކަޒުގައި މިއަދު ހަވީރު 6:30 ގައެވެ.

މިބައްދަލުވުމުގައި ސެކްރެޓަރީ ޖެނެރަލް ދެއްކެވި ވާހަކަފުޅުގައި، ދުނިޔޭގެ ފެންވަރުގައި އެންމެ ބޮޑަށް ބަހުސްކުރެވެމުންދާ މައްސަލަތައް ކަމަށްވާ ކްލައިމެޓް ޗޭންޖާއި، ސަސްޓެއިނަބަލް ޑިވެލޮޕްމަންޓްގެ މައްސަލަތަކުގައި ދިވެހި ރާއްޖެއިން އަދާ ކުރަމުންގެންދާ އިސްދައުރަށް ތައުރީފް ކުރައްވައި މަރުހަބާ ވިދާޅުވިއެވެ.

މިނިސްޓަރ އާސިމްގެ ވާހަކަފުޅުގައި ރާއްޖޭގެ ސިޔާސީ މާހައުލާ ގުޅޭގޮތުން ސެކްރެޓަރީ ޖެނެރަލްއަށް މައުލޫމާތު އެރުއްވިއެވެ. ސެކްރެޓަރީ ޖެނެރަލްގެ ވާހަކަފުޅުގައި، ސިޔާސީ ޕާޓީ ތަކާއެކު ބާއްވާ މަޝްވަރާތަކުގައި އދ. އިން އަބަދުވެސް ރާއްޖެއަށް މަދަދުދީ، އެހީތެރިވެދޭނެ ކަމުގެ ޔަގީންކަން ދެއްވިއެވެ.

en.title: Dr. Abdul Kalam’s legacy as a leader of firm conviction and profound knowledge will inspire generations of South Asians for many years to come – President Yameen
en.body:
30 July 2015, Male';

President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom has on Thursday signed the Book of Condolence honoring the former Indian President, Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam.

“The former President’s legacy as a leader of firm conviction and profound knowledge will inspire generations of South Asians for many years to come. My people join me in extending our profound sympathy to the Government and neighbourly people of India, at this time of national mourning,” President Yameen wrote in the condolence book.

Vice President Ahmed Adheeb Abdul Ghafoor also signed the Book of Condolence honoring the former President of India.

The condolence book is placed at the Indian High Commission.

en.title: New Japanese Ambassador call on the Foreign Minister
en.body:
29 July 2015, Male’;

H. E. Mr. Kenichi Suganuma, the new Ambassador of Japan to the Republic of Maldives has called on Foreign Minister Dunya Maumoon.

At the meeting held at the Foreign Ministry this morning, the Foreign Minister welcomed the Ambassador and congratulated him on his new appointment. Foreign Minister Dunya also discussed ways on further strengthening the close bilateral relations between the Maldives and Japan and highlighted the historical bonds of friendship between the peoples of the Maldives and Japan.

The Ambassador conveyed his best wishes on the occasion of the golden jubilee of independence of the Maldives and expressed his keen interest towards working with the Government to strengthen the close bond between the Maldives and Japan.

Foreign Minister Dunya was accompanied by Mr. Ibrahim Shaheeb, Additional Secretary and Ms. Aishath Azeema, Joint Secretary at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

ENDS.

en.title: New Japanese Ambassador presents credentials to the President
en.body:
29 July 2015, Male';

The new Ambassador of Japan designated to the Maldives, H.E. Mr Kenichi Suganuma has presented his credentials to President Abdulla Yameen Abdul Gayoom, on Wednesday morning.

At the ceremony held at the President’s Office to present the credentials, President Yameen congratulated Ambassador Suganuma on the commencement of his term. Meeting the new Ambassador afterwards, the President and the Ambassador discussed ways to further strengthen ties between the Maldives and Japan.

The President thanked the Japanese Government for their continuous assistance provided to the Maldives in all areas, especially for their aid following the 2004 tsunami. The President also briefed the Ambassador on the progress of the Hulhumale development project, and noted the increase in Japanese tourists visiting the Maldives.

At the meeting, the Japanese Ambassador commended President Yameen for his vision for the dveloment of the country. He further assured the President of Japan’s continued support and assistance to the Maldives.

The meeting was attended by Minister of Foreign Affairs, Hon. Dunya Maumoon, and Minister at the President’s Office, Hon. Mohamed Hussain Shareef.

ENDS

en.title: Japanese Ambassador calls on the Vice President
en.body:
29 July 2015, Male';

Japanese Ambassador designated to the Maldives, H.E. Kenichi Sunganuma, has paid a courtesy call on Vice President Ahmed Adheeb Abdul Ghafoor. The meeting was held this afternoon at the President’s Office.

The Vice President and the Japanese Ambassador noted the good relations between Maldives and Japan, and discussed ways to further enhance relations between both countries.

At the meeting, the Japanese Ambassador, Kenichi Sunganuma congratulated Vice President Ahmed Adheeb Abdul Ghafoor on his assumption of office. Further speaking at the meeting, the Ambassador assured President Yameen of Japan’s commitment to contribute to the long term development projects in Maldives.

en.title: Minister Dunya signs book of condolence for Former President of India, H.E. Dr. Kalam
en.body:

en.body:

President of the Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka H.E. Mr Maithripala Sirisena, concluded his State Visit to the Maldives this morning. en.title: Maldives and Palestine Sign Agreement to Advance Ties
en.body:
27 July 2015, Male’:

The Government of Maldives and the State of Palestine, with a view to further strengthening and diversifying bilateral relations between the two countries, signed an Agreement today at a ceremony held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The Minister of Foreign Affairs of the State of Palestine HE Dr. Riad Malki, and Minister of Foreign Affairs HE Ms. Dunya Maumoon signed the Agreement.

In her remarks following the signing, Minister Dunya reiterated the Maldives’ continued support to Palestine. The Minister also expressed confidence that the Intergovernmental Joint Committee will provide an excellent platform for both countries to discuss ways to further strengthen and diversify bilateral cooperation, as well as collaboration in regional and international affairs.

Also speaking after the ceremony Palestinian Minister Malki also conveyed the strong support of the people and Government of Palestine and and expressed his strong commitment to advance bilateral ties between the two countries.

The signing ceremony was witnessed by senior officials of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and the Ambassador of Palestine to the Maldives.

HE Dr. Riad Malki also paid a courtesy call on Minister Dunya, after the signing ceremony. Discussions during the meeting focused on the operational aspects of the Joint Committee that would be established under the Agreememt.

The meeting was attended by Ambassador-at-Large Mr. Abdullah Hameed, Additional Secretary Ms. Liusha Zahir and Assistant Director Ms. Maryam Bassama Farooq.

en.title: Message by Minister of Foreign Affairs H E Dunya Maumoon on the occasion of Golden Jubilee of Independence
en.body:
26 July 2015, Male’,

I extend my heartiest felicitations and sincere warm wishes to all Maldivians on the Golden Jubilee of our Independence. I am indeed very proud of our national achievements over the last half-century!

It also gives me great pleasure to welcome all foreign dignitaries who have arrived to join in our celebrations.

On this historic day, it is our duty to reflect on the sacrifices of our forefathers and reminisce on their vision for our nation in safeguarding our independence and sovereignty. We will always remember their determination to serve and protect the Maldives with courage and loyalty. Their memories will forever be carved in our hearts and spirits.

To attain greater national development and prosperity it is incumbent upon us to strengthen our bonds of friendship with the rest of the world. Our efforts in the international arena over the last fifty-years have put the Maldives’ on the world map- as a moderate Islamic country committed to consolidating its young democracy. Hence, our march towards progress should be premised on protecting our Islamic identity and advancing the economic resilience of all Maldivians. It should also be powered by a collective determination to stand tall in the international community; as a responsible global citizen and as an advocate for the security of small states. Our achievements in bringing the issues of climate change to the forefront of the global discourse will undoubtedly write our history and it will also shape our future.

I strongly believe that the course set for our nation by His Excellency President Abdullah Yameen Abdul Gayoom will take us to new democratic and economic horizons. As such it is my prayer that may the Almighty Allah protect our sovereignty and grant us the fortitude to stay independent  forever.

We stand together in writing the chapters of our national story: the Maldivian Story.

en.title: Palestinian Special Envoy & FM Arrives for Jubilee Celebrations
en.body:

en.title: Maldives Embassy in China hosts reception to celebrate 50th Anniversary of Independence
en.body:
Beijing, China, 18 July 2015;

A special reception was hosted by the Embassy of Maldives in China to celebrate the  50th Anniversary of Independence of Maldives. The Assistant Minister of Foreign Affairs of China, Mr Liu Jianchao was the Guest of Honour at the reception.

Speaking at the Reception Ambassador Mohamed Faisal looked at the history of Maldives independence and noted that independence provided the opportunity for Maldives to embark on nation building and modernization. Ambassador Faisal noted that over the past 50 years successive Governments have pursued policies crafted to maintain the independence of Maldives, establishing systems of governance, institutions and mechanisms, to create opportunities for the Maldivian people to advance their lives and together build a modern nation.

Ambassador Faisal also focused on the economic reform programme of President Yameen aimed at making Maldives a resilient and economically self-sufficient country. “In 1965, Maldives gained political independence, and now under the visionary leadership of President Yameen, Maldives is looking to revolutionise the country’s economic landscape so that we will also be masters of our own economic destiny”, said Ambassador Faisal.

“While Maldives is a very beautiful country, admired by all, the goal of President Yameen’s Government is to also make it the best place to do business in Asia and attract the investment needed to realize the collective vision of the people – that of a prosperous, self-sufficient and economically independent Maldives”, said the Ambassador.

During his remarks Ambassador Faisal also highlighted the close relations between the Maldives and China, and noted that as Maldives celebrates the golden jubilee of independence, Maldives and China are also enjoying a golden period of relations. He noted that the relationship was built on mutual trust, respect, and win-win cooperation.

The Reception was attended by Ambassadors and diplomats, senior officials of the Chinese Government,  members and heads of several Chinese companies, organizations and media.

The Reception hosted with the assistance of companies in China and Maldives, also featured Maldivian food and music. Special Maldivian gift packs were presented to invitees which included a gift containing sand from the Maldives. A lucky draw was also held with a grand prize of a holiday package in the Maldives.

en.title: Message by the Minister of Foreign Affairs on the occasion of Eid al-Fitr

I extend heartfelt felicitations to all Maldivians and fellow Muslims around the world on the occasion of Eid al-Fitr, 1436. As we join hands around the world to celebrate this auspicious occasion, we are reminded of the profound acknowledgement that we are one humanity, one global community. en.title: Statement by Minister of Foreign Affairs on the coming into force of the new Penal Code
en.body:
16 July 2015, Male’,

Today marks a new dawn in the national history of the Maldives. The coming in to force of the new Penal Code today, indeed is a momentous milestone that will carve its own place in the criminal justice system of the country.

I am extremely proud that with this significant move, the Maldives becomes the first Islamic country to bring into place a penal system that is in line with the principles enshrined in both Islamic Shari’ah and the Common Law.

With its comprehensive compendium of penal laws of the country, the Code illustrates the Government’s conviction to protect and promote human rights, eradicate discrimination and widen the sphere of economic, political and civil rights to Maldivians.  It is also reflective of our strong commitment to consolidate democracy and reinforce a just society that is steered towards new horizons.

It gives me a great honour to extend warm congratulations to His Excellency President Yameen Abdul Gayoom for enacting this important piece of legislation during his tenure and for his conviction in our nation as a strong and independent State. It is also my privilege to extend deepest appreciation to former President Maumoon Abdul Gayoom for commissioning the draft Bill in 2006 and for his extraordinary vision for a strong democratic society.

The Maldives will not rest on its laurels and will continue to move forward. Maldivians remain proud of their national story and we stand together to script new chapters in the story that reads; The Maldives.

ENDS

en.title: Government warmly welcomes the constructive remarks made by The Honourable Ian Paisley at the British Parliament
en.body:
London, UK,, 16 July 2015;

The Government of Maldives welcomes the constructive remarks made by The Honourable Ian Paisley, MP, who is also a member of the Maldives All Party Parliamentary Group, at the UK Parliament.

Speaking at the House of Commons on Tuesday, 14 July, in response to remarks made by Minister of State at the Foreign Office, Mr Hugo Swire, Mr Paisley emphasised the severity of the offence committed by former President Nasheed while in office, and appealed to the UK Government to allow the judicial process to run its course.

 “….the kidnapping and holding of a judge is a very serious affair, and we should therefore allow the rule of law to determine the outcome of the case of former President Nasheed.” said Mr Paisley.

Mr Paisley then went on to suggest that the main focus of the UK Government’s foreign policy in the Maldives should be on improving trade relations instead of intervening in the domestic judicial process.

The Government of Maldives once again reiterates that Mr Nasheed has not been the victim of a politicised process and that law cannot be applied selectively. The rule of law must apply to any person alleged to have committed a criminal offence, irrespective of their political status.

Ends

en.title: Maldives calls on the international community to address the key financing challenges faced by Small Island Developing States
en.body:
16 July 2015, Addis Ababa

Speaking at the Third International Conference on Financing for Development, His Excellency Mr Mohamed Jaleel, Senior Advisor to the Minister of Finance and Treasury highlighted that for our ambitious declarations to be realized and to yield benefits, commensurating means of implementation must be ensured.

Also speaking on behalf of the Alliance of Small Island States (AOSIS), which the Maldives currently chairs, Mr Jaleel alluded to the challenges faced by SIDS due to their small economies often oriented around single industries, small size and limited capacity to mobilise domestic resources, challenges faced due to high dispersion, isolation and limited natural resources, and the ensuing high cost to deliver essential services. Further, he also noted that adverse impacts of climate change and natural disasters on SIDS.

While SIDS continue to require high levels of finance for their sustained economic growth, they receive little ODA, and are often not eligible for concessionary financing, face high debt burdens, and have high risk ratings which expose them to very high cost of borrowing. And though SIDS are recognized as being on the frontlines to the impacts of climate change, access to climate financing is limited due to limited capacity, complex rules of compliance, application procedures, a donor bias towards mitigation and unfulfilled commitments.

This is why, Mr Jaleel stated, that SIDS have invited all stakeholders to partner with them in SIDS specific, genuine, and durable partnerships that are based on mutual respect and benefits, to achieve the sustainable development goals.

The Third International Conference on Financing for Development is taking place ahead of the historic Summit to adopt the Post-2015 Development Agenda, which includes the Sustainable Development Goals that will follow the Millennium Development Goals. During the conference the Maldives delegation spoke at the Round Table discussion on Global Partnership and the three dimensions of sustainable development, and attended side events on the financing challenges faced by SIDS, climate change, disaster resilient investments for Sustainable Development and special challenges faced by Middle Income Countries.

His Excellency Mr Mohamed Jaleel is accompanied by Mr. Jeffrey Salim Waheed, Deputy Permanent Representative of Maldives to UN, Ms. Mariyam Midhfa Naeem, Counsellor at the Maldives Mission to UN and Ms. Aishath Fareena, Desk Officer at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
